findings.title: New test asserts no tracked .pyc, but main likely still tracks tools/__pycache__ from #6
findings.claim: test_bytecode_is_ignored_and_untracked fails if any .pyc is tracked. This PR deletes the 17 files under scripts/ and tests/ only. The PR6-F4 decision row (merged in #7) says #6 committed a 'new tools/__pycache__ file' and that 'the untracking is left to the owner'. The PR description's claim that '#7 removes the same files' contradicts that row. If main still tracks tools/__pycache__/make_toc*.pyc, CI on main goes red the moment this PR merges, and the test's own docstring (17 files from #4) would be incomplete. This branch does not contain main's #6/#7 code (no tools/make_toc.py or tests/test_make_toc.py here), so the test could not catch it on the branch.
findings.evidence: reviews/decisions.md row PR6-F4: 'F4: Compiled bytecode is committed: new tools/__pycache__ file and a modified scripts/review_harness pyc ... The `git rm -r --cached` and `rm` commands were denied in this session ... So the untracking is left to the owner'. PR description: '#7 removes the same files, and both PRs merge cleanly in either order.' Diff deletes only scripts/review_harness/**/*.pyc and tests/__pycache__/*.pyc. Glob of this checkout shows no tools/ or tests/test_make_toc.py files. I could not run `git ls-tree origin/main` (blocked), so main's tree is unverified.
findings.proposed_change: Run `git ls-tree -r --name-only origin/main | grep '\.pyc$'`. If it lists tools/__pycache__/*.pyc, merge main into this branch and add `git rm -r --cached tools/__pycache__` to the PR so the test passes on the merged tree; then correct the PR description (and the '17 files' docstring if the count changes). If main is clean, only the PR description needs fixing. Test: `python -m pytest -q tests -k bytecode` on the merge result.

findings.title: cell() truncates after wrapping links, so a cut can leave an unbalanced backtick
findings.claim: MD_LINK wrapping adds two characters per link before the length check. In the summary table the reason is cut at 200 characters (`cell(r['reason'], 200)` in render_summary), so a reason longer than that with a link near the cut ends in an opening backtick followed by '…'. GitHub renders an unmatched backtick literally, so this is cosmetic. The comment in decision_rows ('nothing is cut here') now holds only because the margins (600 vs 800, 300 vs 400) exceed 2× the realistic link count.
findings.evidence: respond.py: `text = MD_LINK.sub(r"`\1`", text)` runs before `return text if len(text) <= limit else text[: limit - 1] + "…"`; render_summary calls `cell(r['reason'], 200)`; respond_schema.json caps reason at 600 and changes at 300.
findings.proposed_change: Truncate before wrapping (move the MD_LINK.sub after the length check, re-wrapping only the kept text), or skip a link that would straddle the cut. Add a case to test_cells_quote_markdown_links_as_code with limit=20 and a link crossing the cut, asserting the output has an even number of backticks.

findings.title: BACKLOG has no PR6-F4 untracking item that the decision row says exists

Since this PR performs the untracking, the item (if it exists on main) should be removed with a note rather than silently lost, and the CHANGELOG line should say this closes PR6-F4.
